classification.difficultyReason: Translate the supplied unit-circle positions into cosine and sine coordinates using exact reference-angle values and quadrant signs; the diagram identifies S as lying clockwise from OA.

content.prompt:
The points $P,Q,R,S$ are on the unit circle. $A(1,0)$ and $O$ is the origin. Find the exact coordinates of $P,Q,R,S$ if:

$\angle AOP=60^{\circ}$, $\angle AOQ=120^{\circ}$, $\angle AOR=240^{\circ}$, $\angle AOS=30^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Unit circle with positive axis arrowheads, radii to four marked points, labels P, Q, R, S and A, and numeric labels 1 and −1. The Cartesian-origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: P is at 60°, Q at 120°, R at 240° and S at 330°. S lies 30° clockwise from OA.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure contains point locations and names, but no coordinate answers.

answer.worked:
On the unit circle, $(x,y)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. The diagram places $S$ in quadrant IV, so its directed angle is $330^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}P&=(\cos60^{\circ},\sin60^{\circ})\\&=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\Q&=(-\cos60^{\circ},\sin60^{\circ})\\&=\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\R&=(-\cos60^{\circ},-\sin60^{\circ})\\&=\left(-\frac12,-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\S&=(\cos30^{\circ},-\sin30^{\circ})\\&=\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},-\frac12\right)\end{aligned}$
